Reference Text: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses. The nicely layed out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family. message.content:
Pebble Spring arrived in the city with wide curious eyes.
The paved streets made the ground feel safe.
The intricate bridges seemed like songs carved in stone.
The houses stood close together and welcomed the travelers.
Stone walls formed shelters from the weather.
Each wall also carried the memory of many families.
They decided to study housebuilding.
An old staff gave them a touch of arcane magic.
The magic helped them shape timber without straining their arms.
Pebble Spring measured every beam before it touched the wall.
They learned how a door should swing into a room.
They learned how a window could keep the wind at bay.
They learned how a roof could shed the rain.
They watched the city masons and asked many questions.
The masons answered with patient smiles.
Pebble Spring practiced until their hands remembered the craft.
They raised a small shelter by the river.
They made its walls sturdy and its lines gentle.
The shelter smelled of wet pine and warm dust.
A few neighbors stopped by and praised the roof.
Pebble Spring smiled and listened to their praise.
They felt that the mortal city had a kind and patient heart.
They promised to keep building until the last stone was true.
The final observer very carefully checked each old stone wall near the quiet town gate after the long rain and found that the morning sun made the surface appear a bit uneven and oddly spotty in the light.
